pairs.evidence: src/lib/org/followups.ts:298 The fix prompt types out the integrity guard's gate-config list by hand instead of deriving it from the guard, and it has drifted again. It omits `codecov.yml`, `.golangci.yml`, `sonar-project.properties` and `.coveragerc`, all of which GATE_CONFIG_BASENAME in src/lib/local/lane-gate-diff.ts:146 voids, and no test ties the two lists together. So a lane that follows the brief exactly can still have a whole cycle voided, a drift the comments at lines 283-295 already record three times.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/org/followups.ts:298 A volatile fact inlined into the brief instead of rendered from the artifact that knows it, and it is stale today: four entries the guard voids are missing from the prose. The dated 'Measured 2026-10-xx' comments above it follow the technique, but the list itself does not.

src/lib/org/followups.ts:296 The rule lives in a deterministic gate (lane-gate-diff.ts) that diffs the artifact, and the brief names that gate so the agent works with it rather than against it. The drift in the restated list is booked under instruction-freshness.

src/lib/org/followups.ts:277 "Could not" and "would not" are reported differently: a missing shell or network becomes a distinct SKIPPED reason instead of a sharper instruction. The rule is sent only to lane sessions (line 600), because the human's terminal agent does have those capabilities.
src/lib/org/followups.ts:568 Two restraint lines were removed on measured evidence (comment at lines 551-559) and replaced with an explicit amplifier that licenses larger changes.
src/lib/org/followups.test.ts:252 Behavioural pins on the brief include the permissive branch, not only the prohibitions, so a compressing rewrite that drops the permission goes red.

pairs.registryProposal: Both instruction-freshness and enforcement-demotion are written for a hand-authored repo file. When the 'instruction file' is a brief generated in code that restates a gate's rule set (as here), the natural remedy is a parity test between the brief's text and the gate's own constant, or rendering the list from that constant. Neither technique says so for programmatically assembled briefs.
